morning.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
morning.body: Mortgage rates: 7.18% published 2026-11-05, modeled 7.31% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.98% (+10 bp). MBS: -14.00 ticks. Rate bias: Worsening. The mortgage spread is 234 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Consumer Price Index on 11-12, Core CPI on 11-12. Biggest risk: Consumer Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: protect anything closing inside 30 days and expect reprice risk intraday

eod.title: END OF DAY REVIEW
eod.what_moved: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 4.98% (+10 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.31%.
eod.why: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.98%, +10 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -6 bp. That breaks down exactly: -14 bp from Treasuries and +8 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 234 bp, which is normal and sits at the 66th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 26 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.
eod.reprice_caveat: Real reprice detection needs a live MBS feed. This is inferred from the modeled tick move.
eod.expectations_change: The 2-year moved +17 bp, which means the market firmed its expected path for Fed policy.
